findings.title: Explain the Brownian particle and model terms before using them
exactExcerpts: If a Brownian particle is in classical thermal equilibrium with the surrounding liquid, and energy is shared according to the equipartition model for motion through space, its average kinetic energy is described by formula $(3-15)$.
In the ideal Brownian diffusion model that neglects inertia, a path has no ordinary instantaneous velocity.
findings.observation: The scientific qualifications are sound, but the section never tells the young reader what a Brownian particle is or what motion is being described. It then uses equipartition, kinetic energy, finite-time versus instantaneous velocity, and inertia without a usable definition. 'Energy is shared' does not explain which motions share the energy or that the equality is an average rather than a claim about every instant. The long conditional sentence introduces several prerequisites at once. The footnote's important distinction between an ideal model and real particles therefore requires adult explanation.
findings.requiredChange: Add brief plain-language first-use explanations within these existing blocks: a tiny suspended particle whose irregular motion is associated with uneven molecular impacts; motion energy for movement through space rather than rotation; equipartition as equal average energy for the independent spatial directions in this model; instantaneous as at one moment versus displacement during an observation interval; and inertia as the finite-mass particle's resistance to a change of motion. Split the long condition into short connected sentences. Retain every classical-equilibrium, mass, resistance, size, observation-time, and short-time qualification.
findings.notARequestedScienceReversal: Do not restore the raw textbook's absolute impossibility of measuring velocity or its mass-alone visibility claim. Do not identify the observed displacement divided by elapsed time with equilibrium RMS speed.

findings.title: Give the apparatus geometry and rotation quantities plain-language referents
exactExcerpts: The apparatus has two concentric cylinders, $A$ and $B$, rigidly connected so that they rotate together (Figure $52$).
In the textbook's approximation, atoms fly radially in straight lines at constant speed.
The deposit is therefore shifted from the endpoint of the radius corresponding to slit $O$.
findings.observation: The retained hardware and formulas are correct, but concentric cylinders, axis, angular speed, radially, and arc length are not defined in the English. The reader must infer that the radii run from the common center to the respective walls and that the clock begins at slit crossing, rather than at departure from the central wire. The 'endpoint of the radius' phrase also fails to name the moving wall reference and the atom's impact point. The retained fig-53 text inventory identifies these as D and D-prime, but the English caption and explanation never explain D-prime. This is a text-to-reference comprehension gap, not a defect in the approved geometry.
findings.requiredChange: Add short prose glosses: the cylinders are nested around the same central line; an axis is that central line; angular speed describes how quickly the apparatus turns; radial flight is outward from the center; and the wall arc is a curved distance along the wall. Explicitly name the inner and outer radii as center-to-wall distances, not diameters, and explain that the flight time starts as the atom passes the slit. In the figure-53 prose or existing caption, identify the current slit-aligned wall point D and the impact point D-prime, keeping their separation as the wall shift rather than the atom's path. No image, geometry, or figure asset change is requested.
findings.notARequestedScienceReversal: Keep the cylinders rigidly connected and rotating together, slit O on the inner wall, the collision-free radial straight-flight approximation, and the distinction between wall arc and radial flight distance.
findings.figureContextApplicability: PASS for the retained scientific roles; child-readable textual definitions need revision.

findings.title: Gloss the opening formula's physical conditions
exactExcerpts: Equation $(3-15)$ can be used to calculate a statistical measure of molecular speed for a classical ideal gas in thermal equilibrium.
Here, the mass is that of one molecule, speeds are measured in a frame where the gas as a whole is at rest, and temperature must be the absolute temperature in kelvins:
findings.observation: The necessary limitations are present but delivered as several unexplained technical labels. An independently reading eight-year-old is not told what makes this an ideal-gas model, what thermal equilibrium means here, what viewpoint 'frame' denotes, or how an absolute-temperature scale differs from a Celsius reading. These conditions are essential to using the formulas, not optional historical vocabulary. This finding concerns access to the correct conditions, not their scientific validity.
findings.requiredChange: Provide compact plain-language reminders for the simplified ideal-gas/classical model, a settled thermal-equilibrium state, the viewpoint moving with the gas as a whole, and kelvin temperature measured from absolute zero. Associate the one-molecule mass and absolute temperature with their existing symbols in prose. Keep the original formulas, notation, and numbers; no new derivation or invented exercise is needed.
findings.notARequestedScienceReversal: Do not remove the classical, ideal-gas, equilibrium, rest-frame, kelvin, or single-molecule-mass restrictions to make the passage shorter.

findings.title: Explain speed distribution and instrument sampling rather than only invoking them
exactExcerpts: The measured result must be interpreted using the distribution of speeds and how the instrument selects atoms.
The silver band represents atoms selected by the instrument, so its position and width must be interpreted using the speed distribution.
findings.observation: The warning correctly prevents a band position or arbitrary average from being called RMS, and the later sentence correctly links different speeds with different shifts. However, 'distribution' and 'selected by the instrument' remain unexplained instructions. The child is not given the simple meaning of a distribution or the reason the collected beam is not automatically a representative average of every atom in the gas. The central experimental caveat can be repeated without being understood.
findings.requiredChange: Explain in plain language that a speed distribution describes how many atoms have the different speeds, and that the recorded silver consists only of atoms admitted through the slit and collected on the wall. State that such a selected sample and the way it is recorded need interpretation before comparison with the gas's RMS speed. Retain the existing flight-time/shift relation. Do not invent a universal weighting formula or claim that the band peak, width, or arithmetic average directly measures RMS.

topicObservations.topic: Mean square, RMS, arithmetic mean, vector velocity, and textbook bar notation
topicObservations.observation: The average squared speed is distinguished from its square root. The square-average-root recipe is explicit. The nonstandard bar over v is expressly identified as the textbook's RMS convention, not an arithmetic mean or a velocity-vector mean. No claim that every molecule has the quoted speed is made. The introductory physical-condition vocabulary needs the glosses in N35-EN-03, but the RMS distinction itself is explained.

topicObservations.topic: Classical ideal-gas, equilibrium, kelvin, rest-frame, and one-molecule mass conditions
topicObservations.observation: All requested validity restrictions are retained. m belongs to one molecule; mu=m N_A and k=R/N_A carry the source's two equivalent forms. The rest frame excludes bulk-flow kinetic energy. The English explicitly prohibits direct use of the Celsius number. This is a translational thermal-speed relation, not a statement about all internal modes of a diatomic molecule.

The source's 0 degrees Celsius, nitrogen molar mass 0.028 kg/mol, and speeds 500 and 1800 m/s are unchanged. 'Using the textbook's precision' properly identifies the rounded values. The kelvin reminder and group-statistic caveat are retained; the displayed equal signs are not silently reinterpreted as high-precision measurements.

topicObservations.topic: Historical surprise, room smell, diffusion, path length, and air currents
topicObservations.observation: The nineteenth-century surprise and artillery comparison are attributed to the textbook, not asserted as newly established priority history. Tens of seconds is explicitly a scenario estimate, not a universal diffusion time. Thermal speed is separated from room-scale smell spreading and air currents are acknowledged. Collision-model zigzags and AB distinguish accumulated path length from net displacement without claiming directed slow motion or an actual measured Brownian track.

Stern and 1920 remain the raw source's experimental account; no first-ever, priority, or Stern-Gerlach assertion was added. The heated wire is platinum coated with silver. Evaporation produces silver atoms, not silver molecules or platinum vapor. Pumping reduces residual-gas collisions, and the outer wall at room temperature receives the deposit.

topicObservations.topic: Fixed connection, concentric cylinders, slit, and radii versus diameters
topicObservations.observation: Fixed means the cylinders are rigidly connected, not permanently stationary: the English correctly says they rotate together. A is inner and B outer; C lies on the common axis; slit O is on the inner wall. R_A and R_B are used as radii and their difference is the modeled radial flight distance. No diameter, additional outer slit, measured drawing ratio, or hidden apparatus is invented.

topicObservations.topic: Radial collision-free flight and the rotation model
topicObservations.observation: Straight, constant-speed radial flight and approximate absence of collisions are explicitly textbook approximations. The apparatus turns during the slit-to-wall time while the atom's flight is not asserted to co-rotate. The formulas use the radii difference and are not presented as an exact law for all atom trajectories.

topicObservations.topic: Wall arc s versus atom flight path and uppercase S
topicObservations.observation: s is expressly the rotation-induced arc along the outer inner wall, not the atom's flight distance. The separate radial distance supplies v=(R_B-R_A)/t and elimination of t preserves the source expression. Capital S is retained from p0089#6 and explicitly denotes the same wall-shift quantity as lowercase s. It is not treated as another variable, an erratum, or a separate path length.

topicObservations.topic: Speed distribution, band position/width, sampling, and RMS
topicObservations.observation: Different speeds lead to different flight times and shifts. Band position and width refer to an instrument-selected atom population; an arbitrary position or arithmetic mean is not equated with RMS. Agreement is carefully framed as the textbook's support for kinetic theory, rather than the apparatus directly proving every displayed statistical formula.

topicObservations.topic: Brownian equipartition, particle mass, and translational kinetic energy
topicObservations.observation: The particle formula uses M, not the molecular mass m. Classical thermal equilibrium and equipartition for motion through space retain the approved Chinese restriction to translational motion. The temperature/mass comparison is conditional on other conditions being fixed. The passage does not extend the formula to every observed diffusion speed or to rotational/internal energy; N35-EN-01 asks for that distinction to be expressed more accessibly.

topicObservations.topic: Brownian visibility, drag, particle size, and finite observation time
topicObservations.observation: The thermal RMS estimate is distinguished from a microscope displacement over finite time. Liquid resistance, particle size, and observation time remain explicit. Mass alone is not used to decide existence or observability of motion. The raw source's overstatement about invisibility is not restored.

topicObservations.topic: Inertia, ideal diffusion paths, instantaneous velocity, and measurement limits
topicObservations.observation: No ordinary instantaneous velocity is attributed only to the ideal diffusion model that neglects inertia. Real finite-mass particles require a more complete description on short inertial time scales. 'Cannot be measured' is explicitly not an absolute experimental prohibition. Finite-interval average motion is not identified with thermal RMS speed.

topicObservations.topic: Captions, original objects, source identities, and absence of tasks
topicObservations.observation: All three original figure identities and their captions remain in sequence. Figure 53a/b correctly names slit crossing and later arrival, including t. All 21 source objects remain represented and no question, answer, worked task, new historical claim, or registered erratum was invented. Source Chinese provenance and figure labels are retained metadata, not complete English accessibility.

figures.observation: The English describes a qualitative gas-collision zigzag and contrasts its length with direct AB. This is compatible with the retained A/B endpoints, dashed direct distance, and unmeasured solid path. It neither interprets crossings as counted collisions nor repurposes the figure as a measured Brownian trajectory.

The English identifies nested A/B cylinders, axial C, inner slit O, center-to-wall radii, and stationary band D. It does not treat the outer contour's unlabelled break as another slit or use the drawing as a calibrated diameter/radius ratio. N35-EN-02 requests prose definitions, not geometry changes.

The caption binds panel a to slit crossing and panel b to arrival after t. The straight atom flight and rotating slit-aligned reference are consistent with the retained fixed inertial ray and distinct D/D-prime wall points. s remains a wall arc, not a flight path. No arrow direction, angle, timing, or radius value is inferred from pixels. N35-EN-02 asks the prose to name these existing reference roles.
